circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit is a 5. 281 km track located on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, designed by Hermann Tilke, which has served as the venue for the season-concluding Formula One Abu Dhabi Grand Prix since 2009. The circuit represents the second of four Formula One venues constructed across the Middle East region, following Bahrain's circuit and preceding those in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: Albert Park Circuit is a street track encircling Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, hosting the annual Formula One Australian Grand Prix alongside supporting motorsport events. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 status as a motorsport facility.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, the Red Bull Ring is a 4. 326 km motorsport venue that originally opened as the Österreichring and held the Austrian Grand Prix annually between 1970 and 1987. After undergoing modifications and receiving a new name as the A1-Ring, the circuit resumed hosting the Austrian Grand Prix from 1997 to 2003 before its current branding.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: Baku City Circuit is a street racing venue in Azerbaijan's capital, positioned alongside Baku Boulevard with a lap distance of 6. 003 km, ranking as the fourth-longest F1 track. The circuit hosted its first Grand Prix in 2016 as the European Grand Prix, followed by the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards, managed by Baku City Circuit Operation Company.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Inaugurated in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit spans 5. 412 km and holds the distinction of hosting the maiden Formula One Grand Prix in the Middle East that same year. The venue, which maintains a FIA Grade 1 license and features multiple circuit configurations, regularly accommodates the annual Bahrain Grand Prix alongside other motorsport events including endurance racing and various international series.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, Spain, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of extended straights and diverse corner configurations, making it a versatile test for all-round racing performance. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 license and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstand facilities.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Located near Spa in Belgium's Wallonia region, this 7. 004 km circuit has been hosting the Belgian Grand Prix since 1950, when Formula One's inaugural season took place. The track has maintained continuous Grand Prix events annually from 1985 onwards, with only two exceptions in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve spans 4. 361 kilometres and serves as the permanent home of Canada's Formula One Grand Prix. Beyond its primary use in Formula One, the venue has accommodated various international racing series including sportscar championships and North American open-wheel competitions.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: The Shanghai International Circuit in Jiading has served as the primary venue for China's Formula One Grand Prix, which took place annually from 2004 through 2019 before resuming in 2024. Beyond its role as a Formula One host, the track has expanded its motorsport calendar to include electric racing competitions beginning in 2024.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located near villages in Northamptonshire, Silverstone Circuit is England's premier motorsport venue and the established home of the British Grand Prix since 1987, having previously alternated with other tracks. The circuit holds historic significance as the site of the 1950 British Grand Prix, which inaugurated the inaugural World Championship of Drivers season.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring near Budapest is a 4. 381 km permanent circuit that hosted Formula One's first Eastern Bloc grand prix in 1986, following a recommendation to race in Hungary rather than the Soviet Union. Built in just eight months outside the city, it replaced plans for a street circuit in Budapest's central park and was dedicated to honour János Drapál, a pioneering Hungarian motorcycle racing champion.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Milan in northern Italy, the Monza Circuit is a 5. 793 km track constructed in 1922 as continental Europe's oldest purpose-built racing venue. The circuit regularly hosts the Italian Grand Prix, which has been held there almost continuously since 1949, making it one of the few tracks to appear on every Formula One calendar.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit, a 5. 807 km motorsport venue in Mie Prefecture, Japan, is operated by Honda Mobilityland and accommodates 155,000 spectators. The track has become iconic for hosting Formula One races and the Japanese Super Formula championship.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course threading through Paradise, Nevada, that incorporates the famous Las Vegas Boulevard with its array of major hotels and casinos. The layout features iconic city landmarks such as MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas as it winds through the urban landscape.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is a 4. 304 km circuit honoring two Mexican racing brothers who died in separate accidents. The venue returned to the Formula One calendar in 2015 after a 23-year absence, now hosting the Mexico City Grand Prix on a revised layout distinct from its previous configurations used through 1992.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens that hosts the Miami Grand Prix, which joined the Formula One calendar in 2022. Spanning 3. 363 miles with 19 corners, the track was designed by Apex Circuit Design and allows qualifying speeds averaging 139 mph.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street track that winds through the Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts of Monaco, incorporating the harbour area of this principality. The circuit is typically known as "Monte Carlo" due to the majority of its layout occupying the Monte Carlo neighbourhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Nestled in the dunes north of Zandvoort in the Netherlands, this 4. 259 km circuit returned to Formula One in 2021 after a prolonged absence, hosting the revived Dutch Grand Prix until 2026. The track's distinctive character comes from its dramatic elevation changes and steeply banked corners like Tarzan and Hugenholtz, earning it the nickname "Roller coaster in the Dunes" among fans for its unique challenge through the coastal terrain.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: Situated north of Doha near Lusail, this Qatari motor racing venue spans 5. 419 kilometers with a 1. 068-kilometer main straight and holds FIA Grade 1 certification.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos, a 4. 309 km motorsport venue in São Paulo, Brazil, opened in 1940 and was renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace following his fatal plane crash in 1977. The counterclockwise circuit features additional facilities including a karting track dedicated to fellow Brazilian racer Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street racing venue situated along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea coastline that has hosted the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since its inaugural 2021 event. The circuit also began accommodating Formula E racing from 2025 onwards.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's waterfront district, incorporating the Downtown Core and Kallang planning areas into its route layout.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657-kilometer Spanish circuit is renowned for its balanced design combining extended straights with diverse corner configurations, making it a comprehensive test of driver and machine capabilities. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 license and features seating for approximately 140,700 spectators.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 racing facility situated in Austin, Texas, serving as the primary venue for the United States Formula One Grand Prix. Beyond Formula One, the track hosts multiple major motorsport series including motorcycle racing, sports car championships, and historically accommodated various American racing categories.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon, a Thai-British racer, currently drives for Williams in Formula One under Thailand's national flag.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: The Spanish driver competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, having secured two world championship titles during his 23-season career with Renault in 2005 and 2006, along with 32 Grand Prix victories. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso has achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, including two Le Mans victories and the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship, making him the sole driver to win both a Formula One and World Endurance Championship.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli secured the Formula One World Drivers' Championship with Mercedes in 2026, setting the record as the sport's youngest champion. Since entering the series in 2025, he has claimed nine Grand Prix victories.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently racing for the Haas team.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian driver Gabi Bortoleto competes in Formula One as part of the Audi team. Known for his racing background, he has established himself in the sport's premier championship.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: The Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas, currently racing for Cadillac, has secured two runner-up finishes in the drivers' championship during his 2019 and 2020 campaigns with Mercedes. Over his 13 seasons in the sport, he has claimed 10 race victories.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Colapinto is an Argentine driver currently competing in Formula One with the Alpine team.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan, an Australian driver, competes in the LMP2 category of the Asian Le Mans Series with AF Corse after previous stints in the European Le Mans Series. He holds a reserve driver position with Haas in Formula One, where he has participated in seven Grand Prix events during the 2024-2025 season.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The 2020 Italian Grand Prix victory with AlphaTauri remains a highlight of his career.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Hadjar is a French-Algerian racing driver who races for Red Bull Racing in Formula One, competing under the French flag.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently competing for Ferrari who has achieved a record-tying seven world championship titles matching Michael Schumacher's total. He holds multiple all-time records in the sport, including the most race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races for Audi in Formula One. Beyond his single-seater commitments, he achieved significant success in endurance motorsport by securing victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 while driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand-born racing driver who currently races for Racing Bulls in Formula One.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc, a Monégasque driver, currently races for Ferrari in Formula One. He finished as championship runner-up in 2022 and has accumulated nine race victories throughout his nine seasons in the sport.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish driver competing in the World Endurance Championship with BMW, while also pursuing a part-time NASCAR career with Trackhouse Racing. He previously raced in Formula One across two separate periods, from 2014 to 2020 and again from 2022 to 2024.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British Formula One driver for McLaren, claimed the 2025 World Drivers' Championship while accumulating 14 race victories over his eight-season career in the sport.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon, a French racing driver, most recently drove for Haas in Formula One. His career highlights include a Grand Prix victory at the 2021 Hungarian race when he was competing for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Checo Pérez currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from 15 seasons in the sport. He finished as championship runner-up in 2023 while driving for Red Bull and has claimed six Grand Prix victories throughout his career.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri, an Australian driver, races for McLaren in Formula One where he has accumulated nine Grand Prix victories throughout his four seasons in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Australian driver Daniel Ricciardo competed in Formula One for 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, securing eight race victories during his career. Known by his nickname "the Honey Badger," he established himself as a competitive force throughout his time in the sport before retiring from full-time racing.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell currently races for Mercedes in Formula One, where he has secured eight Grand Prix victories throughout his career spanning multiple seasons.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz Jr. currently races for Williams in Formula One, where he has accumulated four Grand Prix victories over his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American racing driver who previously contested Formula One during the 2023 and 2024 seasons. He currently competes in the FIA World Endurance Championship, driving in the LMGT3 category for Proton Competition, having transitioned from IMSA's LMP2 class with Era Motorsport.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian motorsport competitor who currently drives for Aston Martin in Formula One.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Japanese driver Yuki Tsunoda spent five seasons competing full-time in Formula One between 2021 and 2025 before transitioning to a reserve role for the Red Bull Racing organization and its sister team in 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Dutch-Belgian driver Max Verstappen competes for Red Bull Racing under the Dutch flag and has secured four consecutive World Drivers' Championship titles spanning 2021 to 2024. Over his 12-season career, he has accumulated 74 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu is China's sole Formula One competitor to date, having raced in the series from 2022 through 2024 before transitioning to a reserve role with Cadillac.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: Operating from Enstone since 2021 under the Alpine Racing banner, this team served as Renault's factory operation in Formula One, having transitioned from its previous Renault F1 Team identity to showcase the Alpine sports car marque. The squad remained aligned with Groupe Renault's motorsport ambitions until the manufacturer's withdrawal from the championship at the conclusion of 2025.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British manufacturer, has competed in Formula One through different organizational entities, with the current iteration operating as AMR GP Limited under the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team name.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker Ferrari, stands as Formula One's longest-running and most accomplished team, participating continuously in the World Championship since its inception in 1950. The squad, colloquially referred to as "the Prancing Horse" after its iconic emblem, remains a cornerstone of the sport's history and competitive landscape.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: Gene Haas established this American-licensed Formula One team in 2014, entering the sport for the first time in 2016. Led by team principal Ayao Komatsu since January 2024, the squad replaced the long-serving Guenther Steiner who guided the team from its founding through its initial years of competition.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: Founded in 1970 by Peter Sauber, this Swiss engineering outfit initially excelled in endurance racing, winning Le Mans in 1989 before joining Formula One in 1993. The constructor competed in the championship for over three decades, establishing itself as one of the sport's longest-serving independent teams before being acquired by Audi in 2024 and subsequently ceasing operations.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren is a prominent British Formula One outfit headquartered in Woking that competes under the Mastercard sponsorship banner. The team operates as part of the McLaren Group and is fully owned by Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has competed in Formula One since 1954 as both a constructor and engine supplier, with its current Brackley-based team operating under a German licence. Following a 2022 ownership restructuring, the team is now jointly held by Mercedes-Benz Group, Toto Wolff, and Ineos in equal shares. The team, competing as Mercedes-AMG Petronas, is traditionally known as the "Silver Arrows".

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that began competing in 2024, operating as one of two Red Bull GmbH-owned teams alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with an additional facility near Milton Keynes, the squad serves as the sister team within Red Bull's dual-team Formula One structure.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that commenced operations in 2024 as the second team under Red Bull's ownership, alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with an additional facility near Milton Keynes, the squad functions as a sister team within the Austrian conglomerate's motorsport portfolio.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing is an Austrian-licensed Formula One team headquartered in England and part of the Red Bull GmbH conglomerate, which also operates Racing Bulls. Established in 2005 under Christian Horner's leadership, the team transitioned to Laurent Mekies as team principal in 2025 following Horner's departure.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering is a British Formula One constructor founded in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, succeeding Williams's earlier failed racing venture. Based in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team competes in 2026 under the Atlassian Williams F1 Team name and has established itself as a significant presence in the sport's history.
